title: External invertible global sections over a DVR
statement:
Let $A$ be a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. Let $X,Y$ be quasi-compact separated schemes over $\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-morphism-conventions] whose structure morphisms are flat [def-weil-flat-morphism]. Let $F$ and $G$ be invertible module sheaves on $X$ and $Y$, respectively [def-sc-invertible-module], and put $P=X\times_A Y$ with projections $p_X,p_Y$. The canonical $A$-linear external-section map
$$K_{F,G}:\Gamma(X,F)\otimes_A\Gamma(Y,G)\longrightarrow\Gamma(P,p_X^*F\otimes_{\mathcal O_P}p_Y^*G),\qquad s\otimes t\longmapsto p_X^*s\otimes p_Y^*t,$$
is an isomorphism. Tensor products of sheaves and modules have the meanings of [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. This map is natural for pullback of sections and for isomorphisms of the schemes and invertible sheaves. If a flat affine $A$-group scheme acts on both schemes and linearizes $F,G$, then $K_{F,G}$ commutes with the rational coactions whenever these coactions on the section modules are defined; tensor products on its source carry the diagonal coaction. The assertions allow empty schemes and hold without assuming vanishing of positive coherent cohomology or a base-change theorem for either section module. Here a group scheme over $A$ means a group object in schemes over $\operatorname{Spec}A$: its multiplication, identity and inverse satisfy the group diagrams over that base. If $H$ is the acting affine group, put $C=A[H]$ [def-sfb-affine-coordinate-hopf-algebra]. A rational coaction on an $A$-module $M$ is an $A$-linear map $\rho_M:M\to M\otimes_A C$ satisfying $(\rho_M\otimes1)\rho_M=(1\otimes\Delta)\rho_M$ and $(1\otimes\varepsilon)\rho_M=1_M$. A linearization is an isomorphism $\theta:\operatorname{pr}_X^*F\to a_X^*F$ over $H\times_AX$ satisfying the identity and action cocycle equations, and similarly for $G$; the coactions in the assertion are those induced by these linearizations. Pullback and fibre products use [def-pc-module-pullback, def-pc-fibre-product], and affine spectra use [def-weil-affine-spectrum].

source.place: Tag 0BED, lemma-kunneth, equation-kunneth-on-cech. Agent-formulated DVR degree-zero extension of the two finite-affine-cover equalizer argument, using flatness of torsion-free modules over a DVR; the cited tag itself is over a field, not the integral assertion. The external map and naturality are specified on pure tensors.

proof.text: Choose finite affine open covers $(U_i)_{i\in I}$ of $X$ and $(V_j)_{j\in J}$ of $Y$ by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-finite-affine-open-cover]. Their pairwise intersections $U_{ii'}$ and $V_{jj'}$ are affine by [lem-weil-pbc-separated-affine-open-intersection], applied to the separated structure morphisms with affine target $\operatorname{Spec}A$. Fibre products $W_{ij}=U_i\times_AV_j$ are affine by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]. They cover $P$: a point of $P$ has its two projections in some $U_i,V_j$. Their intersections are $U_{ii'}\times_AV_{jj'}$, by the fibre-product universal property. Invertibility includes quasi-coherence by [def-sc-invertible-module]. Write $E=p_X^*F\otimes p_Y^*G$, $M_i=\Gamma(U_i,F)$, $M_{ii'}=\Gamma(U_{ii'},F)$, $N_j=\Gamma(V_j,G)$, and $N_{jj'}=\Gamma(V_{jj'},G)$.

source.place: Tags 01IT (lemma-basis-affine-opens), 01KP (lemma-characterize-separated), 01I4 (lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes); finite covers as in Tag 0BED

proof.text:
For any affine opens $U\subseteq X,V\subseteq Y$, put $B=\mathcal O_X(U)$, $D=\mathcal O_Y(V)$, $M=F(U)$, $N=G(V)$, and $T=B\otimes_AD$. The affine product formula and [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-affine-sections] identify the two pullback section modules on $U\times_AV$ with $T\otimes_BM$ and $T\otimes_DN$. The pullbacks are quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-quasi-coherent]; thus [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-tensor-product-affine-sections] identifies $E(U\times_AV)$ with $(T\otimes_BM)\otimes_T(T\otimes_DN)$. There is an explicit isomorphism from this module to $M\otimes_AN$ given by
$$((b\otimes d)\otimes m)\otimes((b'\otimes d')\otimes n)\longmapsto bb'm\otimes dd'n.$$
Its inverse sends $m\otimes n$ to $(1\otimes m)\otimes(1\otimes n)$. The balancing relations make both formulas well-defined, and their composites are identities on tensor generators [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Hence the inverse is exactly the local external-section map. These identifications commute with restrictions: restricting $p_X^*m\otimes p_Y^*n$ gives $p_X^*(m|_{U'})\otimes p_Y^*(n|_{V'})$, and tensor generators span. This applies also to affine intersections.

The restriction of a flat morphism to an open subscheme is flat directly from [def-weil-flat-morphism]: at its points the local rings and stalk maps are unchanged. The restricted invertible sheaf is still locally free of rank one. Therefore [lem-sc-flat-invertible-sections-torsion-free] applies to $X$, $Y$, and all the opens just chosen. It makes $\Gamma(X,F)$, $\Gamma(Y,G)$, $M_i,M_{ii'},N_j,N_{jj'}$ torsion-free $A$-modules. By [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], $A$ is a valuation ring. Apply [lem-trf-valuation-torsionfree-flat] to each of these modules: they are flat, with no finite generation assertion. In particular, the first equalizer argument below may tensor with $N_j$ or $N_{jj'}$, and the second may tensor with $\Gamma(X,F)$.

source.place: Tag 0539 (lemma-valuation-ring-torsion-free-flat); torsion-free section argument in more-morphisms.tex Tag 0EX8 (lemma-triviality-generic-fibre-valuation-ring), general-case proof

proof.text:
The sheaf condition [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] says that
$$0\to\Gamma(X,F)\to\prod_iM_i\xrightarrow{d_X}\prod_{i,i'}M_{ii'}$$
is exact, where $(d_Xm)_{ii'}=m_i|_{U_{ii'}}-m_{i'}|_{U_{ii'}}$: a tuple lies in its kernel precisely when its sections glue uniquely. Fix $V=V_j$ or $V_{jj'}$ and set $N=G(V)$. Tensor this row with the flat module $N$. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] it remains exact, and [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-finite-product] identifies its two finite product terms with $\prod_i(M_i\otimes_AN)$ and $\prod_{i,i'}(M_{ii'}\otimes_AN)$. Step 2 identifies the arrow between them with the difference of restrictions for the cover $(U_i\times_AV)_i$ of $X\times_AV$. The sheaf condition for $E$ therefore identifies its kernel with $\Gamma(X\times_AV,E)$. The resulting isomorphism
$$\kappa_V:\Gamma(X,F)\otimes_AG(V)\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(X\times_AV,E)$$
sends $s\otimes t$ to $p_X^*s\otimes p_Y^*t$, since that holds after restricting to every cover member. It commutes with each restriction $V_{jj'}\subseteq V_j$: on $U_i\times_AV_{jj'}$ both composites restrict to the same pure-tensor section, and uniqueness of gluing and generation by pure tensors give equality.

source.place: Tag 0BED (lemma-kunneth), equation-kunneth-on-cech: degree-zero equalizer argument over A with flat N replacing exactness over a field

proof.text:
Apply the same sheaf-condition row to $G$ and its finite cover $(V_j)$:
$$0\to\Gamma(Y,G)\to\prod_jN_j\xrightarrow{d_Y}\prod_{j,j'}N_{jj'}.$$
Tensor on the left with the flat module $L=\Gamma(X,F)$. Exactness [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] and finite-product compatibility [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-finite-product] give kernel $L\otimes_A\Gamma(Y,G)$. By Step 4, the other two terms and their restriction differences identify with the two section products for the cover $(X\times_AV_j)_j$ of $P$. Its sheaf equalizer has kernel $\Gamma(P,E)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Thus the induced map of kernels is an isomorphism. On $s\otimes t$ its restriction to $X\times_AV_j$ is $\kappa_{V_j}(s\otimes t|_{V_j})$, hence is the restriction of $p_X^*s\otimes p_Y^*t$. Consequently the isomorphism is precisely $K_{F,G}$. This uses only equalizers, finite products and flat tensoring, and imposes no positive-cohomology or section-base-change hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 0BED (lemma-kunneth), equation-kunneth-on-cech: second degree-zero equalizer, with flat Gamma(X,F)

proof.text: For maps $u:X'\to X,v:Y'\to Y$ over $A$, and the corresponding pulled-back invertible sheaves, pullback of the section $p_X^*s\otimes p_Y^*t$ is $p_{X'}^*(u^*s)\otimes p_{Y'}^*(v^*t)$. Indeed $(u\times v)$ composed with each projection is the corresponding $u$ or $v$ composed with the new projection [def-pc-fibre-product]; the normalized composition and tensor-pullback isomorphisms of [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor], clause (2), send iterated pullbacks and tensor sections to the asserted sections. Thus the naturality square commutes on every $s\otimes t$, and hence on the whole tensor product [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. The identical calculation with sheaf isomorphisms uses their linearity, replacing $s,t$ by their images. This proves both stated naturality assertions, in particular for isomorphisms of the schemes.

source.place: Tag 01I9 (lemma-widetilde-pullback), functoriality; modules.tex Tag 01CD (lemma-tensor-product-pullback); pure-tensor verification

proof.text:
For the coaction assertion write $H=\operatorname{Spec}C$ and $M=\Gamma(X,F)$, $N=\Gamma(Y,G)$, $Q=\Gamma(P,E)$. Flatness of $H/A$ gives flatness of $C/A$ by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion]. The canonical comparison $c:Q\otimes_AC\to\Gamma(H\times_AP,\operatorname{pr}_P^*E)$ is injective: the sheaf restriction $Q\hookrightarrow\prod_{i,j}E(W_{ij})$ is injective; flat tensoring with $C$ preserves this injection [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact]; and finite-product compatibility and the affine pullback-section formula identify the resulting target with $\prod_{i,j}\Gamma(H\times_AW_{ij},\operatorname{pr}_P^*E)$. The composites with $c$ have exactly those restriction coordinates, so $c$ is injective. This requires no base-change isomorphism for $M$ or $N$.
Write the given coactions as $\rho_M(s)=\sum_a s_a\otimes c_a$, $\rho_N(t)=\sum_b t_b\otimes d_b$. By the meaning of a coaction induced by a linearization, these sums represent the linearized action-pullback sections over $H\times_AX$ and $H\times_AY$. The external linearization is their tensor, pulled back along the two projections and along the same group variable; the normalized composition and tensor-pullback isomorphisms of [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor], clause (2), identify the pullback along $1_H\times p_X$ of a section over $H\times_AX$ (and along $1_H\times p_Y$ over $H\times_AY$) with the corresponding section over $H\times_AP$, and the tensor of pulled-back sections with the pullback of their tensor. Therefore both $c(\rho_Q(K(s\otimes t)))$ and
$$c\left(\sum_{a,b}K(s_a\otimes t_b)\otimes c_ad_b\right)$$
are the tensor of those two linearized sections on $H\times_AP$. Injectivity of $c$ proves equality before applying $c$. The sum is the diagonal coaction on $s\otimes t$, so tensor generators give $\rho_QK=(K\otimes1)\rho_{M\otimes N}$.

source.place: Tags 01I9, 01I8 and 01U5 (flat affine criterion); agent pure-tensor computation of linearized external sections

proof.text: If $X$ or $Y$ is empty, the corresponding global section module is zero, $P$ is empty and $\Gamma(P,E)=0$, by the unique empty-family gluing axiom [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Tensoring a zero module gives zero: all generators $0\otimes t$ or $s\otimes0$ vanish by bilinearity [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Thus $K$ is the unique isomorphism $0\to0$, and the naturality and coaction equations are equalities of zero maps. Empty intersections similarly contribute zero terms to all the finite equalizers above. This also checks the empty-cover case directly.

There are no new nodes. The proof is a degree-zero two-equalizer argument modelled on Stacks Tag 0BED (lemma-kunneth, field case, read). Torsion-freeness comes from lem-sc-flat-invertible-sections-torsion-free (any domain, any flat X), and flatness from valuation ring plus torsion-free (Tag 0539, read at more-algebra.tex l.4925). Flat tensor keeps the sheaf rows exact, with finite products. I checked the T/B/D balancing and both composites of the explicit isomorphism in step 2 by hand. I also tested small cases: X=Y=Spec A, X=Spec Frac A, the empty scheme, and affine X, Y. Each hypothesis is used where needed: separatedness for affine intersections in step 1; flatness of N_j and N_jj' in step 4 and of Gamma(X,F) in step 5; flatness of C, from lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion, for the injectivity of c in step 7. The statement change only adds definitions and is not a weakening. It replaces the field-only def-sc-group-scheme with an inline group object over Spec A, and the only citer (rho-tensor-square-eventual-detection) uses it unchanged. Batch-5 flag: lem-trf-valuation-torsionfree-flat is a Mathlib leaf (Module.Flat.flat_iff_torsion_eq_bot_of_isBezout, Stacks 0539).
